flagship.headline: Texas International Pop Festival closes on Labor Day
flagship.summary_line_1: Led Zeppelin, Janis Joplin, Santana, Sly and the Family Stone, and B.B. King closed out the three-day festival at the former Dallas International Motor Speedway in Lewisville, Texas.
flagship.summary_line_2: It stands as one of 1969's biggest and least remembered festivals, drawing a lineup nearly as stacked as Woodstock two weeks earlier.

events.headline: Texas International Pop Festival closes in Lewisville
events.summary_line_1: The three-day festival at the former Dallas International Motor Speedway wrapped its Labor Day finale with sets from Led Zeppelin, Janis Joplin, Santana, Sly and the Family Stone, and B.B. King.
events.summary_line_2: The lineup rivaled Woodstock's two weeks earlier, yet the festival never earned the same place in popular memory.

image.alt: Texas Historical Commission marker commemorating the Texas International Pop Festival

events.headline: New Orleans Pop Festival wraps its three-day run
events.summary_line_1: The festival at the Pelican State Speedway in Prairieville, Louisiana, closed out its Labor Day weekend with Janis Joplin, the Grateful Dead, Santana, and The Byrds on the bill.
events.summary_line_2: It was one of three major Labor Day festivals running that same weekend, a sign of how fast the outdoor rock festival had become standard summer programming by 1969.

image.alt: New Orleans Pop Festival 1969 promotional artwork
image.credit_text: Creator: Stephen St. Germain, via the Historic New Orleans Collection

events.headline: Sky River Rock Festival closes its second year in Tenino
events.summary_line_1: The second annual Sky River Rock Festival and Lighter Than Air Fair wrapped its Labor Day run in Tenino, Washington.
events.summary_line_2: It was one of the earliest multi-day outdoor counterculture rock festivals in the Pacific Northwest, predating the region's later festival boom.

events.headline: Jimi Hendrix Experience electrifies Red Rocks
events.summary_line_1: The Jimi Hendrix Experience headlined the Colorado amphitheater with Vanilla Fudge, Soft Machine, and Eire Apparent opening, a show originally misprinted for the following night.
events.summary_line_2: It remains one of the era's loudest and most celebrated outdoor bills at a venue still considered one of rock's great stages.

image.alt: Publicity photo of the Jimi Hendrix Experience, 1968

events.headline: The Beatles meet to plan their future without Brian Epstein
events.summary_line_1: Paul McCartney convened the other three Beatles at his London home five days after manager Brian Epstein's death, where the band postponed a planned trip to India and greenlit the self-directed Magical Mystery Tour project.
events.summary_line_2: The meeting marked the moment The Beatles took direct control of their own business affairs for the first time.

image.alt: The Beatles pictured in a 1967 promotional photo for All You Need Is Love
image.credit_text: Capitol Records / Henry Grossman, via Billboard magazine, July 20, 1967

events.headline: Joni Mitchell registers copyright on A Melody In Your Name
events.summary_line_1: Joni Mitchell filed the publishing copyright for her song under her own Gandalf Publishing Company, a small administrative step just ahead of her breakthrough as a major voice of the folk movement.
events.summary_line_2: The registration is a rare paper trail into how early she was already managing her own catalog as a songwriter.

events.headline: The Byrds open an 11-night Whisky a Go Go residency
events.summary_line_1: The folk-rock pioneers began the first night of a headlining run at the Whisky a Go Go on the Sunset Strip in West Hollywood.
events.summary_line_2: The residency landed during the band's shift into their more psychedelic period, a live proving ground for the new material.

events.headline: Ariel Rivera is born in Manila
events.summary_line_1: Jose Ariel Jimenez Rivera was born in Manila, Philippines.
events.summary_line_2: He grew up to become a triple-platinum OPM singer, later known as one of the Philippines' most successful balladeers.

events.headline: Roger Miller's Return of Roger Miller is certified gold
events.summary_line_1: The RIAA certified Roger Miller's breakthrough album gold, marking the first gold certification of his career.
events.summary_line_2: It confirmed his crossover from novelty-leaning country singles into a bona fide commercial force.

image.alt: US vinyl label for Roger Miller's 1965 single King of the Road

events.headline: James Brown debuts Papa's Got a Brand New Bag on Shindig!
events.summary_line_1: James Brown performed his funk-soul crossover hit on the ABC teen-music variety show, showing off the dance moves that defined his live act.
events.summary_line_2: The performance introduced the song's new rhythmic approach to a national television audience for the first time.

image.alt: James Brown performing at Clemson University, 1964

events.headline: Motown renews its EMI licensing deal in Britain
events.summary_line_1: Motown Records signed a three-year renewal of its international licensing and distribution contract with EMI Records in the UK.
events.summary_line_2: The deal laid the groundwork for the dedicated Tamla Motown label that launched in Britain the following year.

image.alt: Hitsville U.S.A., Motown Records' original Detroit headquarters

events.headline: Charlie Robison is born in Houston
events.summary_line_1: Charlie Robison was born in Houston, Texas.
events.summary_line_2: He grew up to become a leading voice of the grittier, raw Texas country movement, later finding mainstream success with I Want You Bad.

image.alt: Charlie Robison performing at South by Southwest, 2007
image.credit_text: Photo: Staff Sgt. Brian Ferguson, U.S. Air Force

events.headline: The Beatles tape Big Night Out at Didsbury Studio Centre
events.summary_line_1: The Beatles taped an appearance on ABC Television's variety show Big Night Out in Manchester, miming From Me To You, She Loves You, and Twist and Shout in front of a live studio audience.
events.summary_line_2: The episode aired across the ITV network less than a week later, part of the wave of TV exposure driving Beatlemania that autumn.

image.alt: The Beatles in Hötorgscity, Stockholm, October 1963

events.headline: Tommy Roe's Sheila hits No. 1
events.summary_line_1: Tommy Roe scored his first US Billboard Hot 100 number one with Sheila, a self-written track carrying an unmistakable Buddy Holly-style vocal hiccup and Peggy Sue-style drumbeat.
events.summary_line_2: It was a re-recording of a song Roe first cut in 1960 with his high school group, The Satins, proof the original arrangement just needed the right studio polish.

image.alt: Tommy Roe pictured in a 1970 trade magazine advertisement

events.headline: Tony Bennett releases My Heart Sings
events.summary_line_1: Tony Bennett released his studio album My Heart Sings on Columbia Records, recorded at CBS's 30th Street Studio in New York.
events.summary_line_2: The album became a standard-bearer for early-1960s vocal pop, featuring the standout Don't Worry 'Bout Me.

image.alt: Composer Harold Arlen and Tony Bennett rehearsing for CBS's The Twentieth Century, 1964

events.headline: Boney James is born in Lowell, Massachusetts
events.summary_line_1: James Oppenheim, later known as Boney James, was born in Lowell, Massachusetts.
events.summary_line_2: He grew up to become a multi-Grammy-nominated smooth jazz saxophonist, songwriter, and producer.

image.alt: Boney James performing at the Jazz Cafe, 2005

events.headline: Art Blakey and the Jazz Messengers release their self-titled LP
events.summary_line_1: The hard-bop group released Art Blakey and the Jazz Messengers on Impulse! Records, recorded with the band temporarily expanded to a sextet.
events.summary_line_2: It was pianist Bobby Timmons's final session with the group before he left to rejoin Cannonball Adderley.

image.alt: Art Blakey performing in concert at the Concertgebouw, Amsterdam, December 1960

events.headline: Arabinda Muduli is born in Khanati, Odisha
events.summary_line_1: Arabinda Muduli was born in Khanati, in India's Khordha district.
events.summary_line_2: He grew up to become a celebrated Odia bhajan singer and lyricist devoted to spiritual devotional music.

events.headline: Aunt Molly Jackson dies at 80
events.summary_line_1: Mary Magdalena Garland, known professionally as Aunt Molly Jackson, died at approximately age 80.
events.summary_line_2: The Appalachian folk singer and union activist had become one of the defining voices of the coal miners' struggles during the Great Depression.

events.headline: Broadway and the West End dim their lights for Oscar Hammerstein II
events.summary_line_1: New York's Times Square lights went dark for one minute and London's West End theater lights dimmed in a synchronized transatlantic tribute to lyricist Oscar Hammerstein II.
events.summary_line_2: The joint gesture honored his massive contributions to musical theater following his death just over a week earlier.

image.alt: Portrait of Oscar Hammerstein II, circa 1920
image.credit_text: New-York Tribune, January 11, 1920, via Library of Congress

events.headline: Joseph Williams is born
events.summary_line_1: Joseph Williams, son of film composer John Williams, was born.
events.summary_line_2: He grew up to front the rock band Toto in the mid-1980s, singing lead on hits including Pamela.

image.alt: Joseph Williams performing with Toto in Örebro, Sweden, 2013
